rounds.text: Finolex Cables Ltd demonstrates exceptional fundamental momentum, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 27% [E17] and a quarterly net profit surge of 53% year-on-year [E68]. The company operates with pristine financial health, carrying a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x alongside a robust current ratio of 8.42x [E38, E39]. Capital allocation and efficiency metrics validate its superior positioning, with an ROCE of 16.0% and an ROA of 11.45% that outpaces the sector benchmark of 6.38% [E8, E12]. Furthermore, institutional sponsorship is expanding with domestic institutions increasing holdings to 16.71% [E44] and overall institutional money flow reading positive [E45], reinforced by a sector tailwind score of +0.68 [E73]. Technical strength matches fundamental execution, evidenced by a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 and a 75.0% twelve-month price return [E52, E53]. conceded: [E46] conceded: [E64]

The market price of ₹1,474 sits 97% of the way up its 52-week range [E2, E5], driven by a 5-year price growth of 25% that completely outpaces its 9% profit growth over the same period [E23, E57]. This disconnect is echoed by a reverse DCF showing the current share price already prices in 12.9% earnings growth, which outstrips the base case assumption of 9.0% [E48]. Furthermore, a standard DCF model establishes an intrinsic value of ₹1,106 per share, leaving a negative margin of safety of -33.3% [E46, E47]. Valuation multiples reinforce this expensive entry point, with the P/E trading at 28.2x, EV/EBITDA at 19.01x against a sector benchmark of 12.72x, and a Price-to-Book ratio of 3.70x [E1, E2, E11]. Underlying cash generation also fails to support the reported earnings, highlighted by a poor cash conversion ratio of 0.07x and negative free cash flow of Rs -105 Cr in Mar 2026, alongside net profit figures that are padded by Rs 382 Cr of other income [E34, E36, E64]. Conceded: the company maintains a clean balance sheet with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x and a rules-based screen score of 88 out of 100 driven by strong recent sales and profit growth [E38, E65, E66, E68].

Conceded: the stock sits 97% of the way up its 52-week range [E5], a standard DCF estimates intrinsic value at ₹1,106 [E46], and the EV/EBITDA ratio of 19.01x trades above the sector benchmark of 12.72x [E11]. However, the bear's valuation concerns ignore the exceptional momentum of a 100 relative-strength rating against the Nifty 500 [E52] and a 75.0% twelve-month price return [E53], supported by a technical setup where the price trades above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E51]. While the bear points to a reverse DCF growth expectation of 12.9% [E48], this is fully backed by recent operating acceleration, including a 27% TTM sales growth [E17], a 29% TTM profit growth [E21], and a rules-based screen scoring 88 out of 100 [E65] driven by 44% YoY sales and 53% YoY net profit increases [E66, E68]. Furthermore, the bear's focus on valuation multiples overlooks the robust fundamentals of an ROA of 11.45% and ROCE of 15.24% that both comfortably beat sector benchmarks [E8, E10]. Conceded: earnings include ₹382 Cr of other income [E64] and cash conversion was 0.07x in Mar 2026 [E34], yet the company remains virtually debt-free with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x [E38] and operates within a Capital Goods sector enjoying a strong tailwind score of +0.68 [E74].

Conceded: the company operates within a Capital Goods sector enjoying a strong tailwind score of +0.68 [E74], and relative strength stands at 100 against the Nifty 500 [E52]. However, the bull's reliance on a 75.0% twelve-month price return [E53] and moving-average configuration [E51] merely underscores a price-led divergence where 5-year share price growth of 25% vastly outpaces 9% profit growth [E57]. Conceded: the rules-based screen scores 88 out of 100 [E65] backed by strong TTM metrics [E17, E21], yet the reverse DCF indicates that today's price already demands an aggressive 12.9% earnings growth against the 9.0% base case [E48]. Furthermore, citing superior ROA of 11.45% and ROCE of 15.24% [E8, E10] ignores that earnings are bloated by ₹382 Cr of other income [E64] and accompanied by a dismal cash conversion ratio of 0.07x with free cash flow at negative ₹105 Cr for March 2026 [E34, E36]. Finally, while being debt-free [E38] is positive, it does not neutralize a valuation where EV/EBITDA of 19.01x heavily exceeds the sector benchmark of 12.72x [E11] while foreign institutional holdings have dropped by 2.12 percentage points [E43].

Conceded: EV/EBITDA of 19.01x exceeds the sector benchmark of 12.72x [E11], and the reverse DCF implies a 12.9% earnings growth rate [E48]. However, the bear's dismissal of returns ignores that the company’s ROA of 11.45%, ROE of 11.73%, and ROCE of 15.24% all materially outperform their respective sector benchmarks of 6.38%, 10.84%, and 12.9% [E8, E9, E10]. Furthermore, complaining about cash metrics overlooks that capital expenditure is primed for delivery, with Capital Work-in-Progress dropping 49.0% down to Rs 107 Cr as capex largely completes and new capacity comes online [E41]. Conceded: foreign institutional holdings dropped 2.12 percentage points [E43], but domestic institutions concurrently increased their holdings by 1.13 percentage points [E44], driving overall institutional money flow into POSITIVE MONEY FLOW territory with a holding change of +0.30 percentage points [E45]. Finally, the rules-based screen explicitly rates the stock 88 out of 100 with a BUY recommendation and medium confidence, fueled by exceptional recent momentum including sales growth of 44% YoY and net profit growth of 53% YoY [E65, E66, E68].

Conceded: the company's ROA, ROE, and ROCE outperform their respective sector benchmarks [E8, E9, E10], and domestic institutions increased their holdings by 1.13 percentage points [E44]. However, citing returns does not erase the fact that the company's earnings include Rs 382 Cr of other income [E64], flattering those very returns, while the 3-year average ROE languishes at a low 13.2% [E63]. Furthermore, pointing to the drop in Capital Work-in-Progress down to Rs 107 Cr [E41] ignores the alarming reality that cash conversion for Mar 2026 sits at a meager 0.07x, with free cash flow plummeting to Rs -105 Cr and operating cash flow representing a paltry 32% of operating profit [E34, E36, E37]. Conceded: institutional money flow shows a positive holding change [E45], but foreign institutions simultaneously dumped 2.12 percentage points of their stake [E43]. Finally, relying on a rules-based screen score of 88 [E65] dismisses the fundamental warning of the reverse DCF, which proves that the current price demands an aggressive 12.9% earnings growth rate that outpaces the company's own 9.0% base-case assumption [E48].
